text:
Anita R: quick check — seeing a consistent NDCG drop for spanish queries after int8 PTQ on the new reranker. anyone else?
Mike L: saw a small dip too, but assumed tokenizer mismatch. how big is the drop?
Anita R: about 6-8% relative in NDCG@10 on the dev set. MRR also down ~4%. this is on the paired spanish test (es-q) we pulled from wiki+support logs.
Sophia K: is this only spanish? what about pt, fr?
Anita R: en/pt/fr look fine (<1% variance). it's only es.
Leon T: could be query normalization differences: accents, lowercasing, or diacritics handling in the tokenizer/normalizer after conversion to int8. did you run token overlap diagnostics?
Anita R: ran a quick diff of token lengths and piece counts for queries vs. documents. nothing obvious. but i did notice slightly more spurious truncation when seqlen rounding happened during batching in quantized runtime.
Mike L: can you paste the eval config? maybe padding/truncation thresholds changed for quantized model pack.
Anita R: sure:
```
model: rerank-small-7b-int8
eval_split: es-dev-2026
max_query_len: 64
max_doc_len: 512
batch_strategy: dynamic_round_up
normalizer: unicode_nfkc + lower
```
Sophia K: dynamic_round_up is tricky — it can push some queries to a different bucket where kv-cache behavior differs. does unquantized model use the same runtime bucketing?
Anita R: unquantized used `dynamic` not `dynamic_round_up`. i swapped to `dynamic` and re-ran a 5k sample, ndcg drop went away (within noise).
Leon T: aha. so it's an interaction between quantized kernels and the rounding policy. probably padding zeros cause alignment differences that change attention layout slightly.
Mike L: any chance this is dataset-specific — es queries might be shorter/contain accents causing different rounding distribution?
Anita R: yes, es queries skew shorter and contain more accented chars, which earlier led to slightly different piece counts after the tokenizer normalizer. rounding pushes many into the next power-of-two bucket.
Sophia K: action items: 1) add a regression test for bucket policy parity between q/int8 and fp16. 2) run len-distribution stratified eval across languages. 3) add tiny prompt-level check for truncation artifacts.
Leon T: i'll add a small simulation to the runtime test harness that checks output parity for same-batched inputs across bucket strategies (fp16 vs int8). should catch future regressions.
Anita R: created a tiny repro notebook and a 1k-sample lang-strat test. uploading to the shared drive and linking in the eval harness.
eval-bot: uploaded artifact: s3://redwood-evals/anon/es-rerank-int8-bucket-repro/1719998888/ (sha256: b7f3...)
Mike L: thanks. one more thought — quantization scale per-layer might interact with embedding normalization. can we snapshot per-layer activations for a few failing queries?
Anita R: yes, i'll hook in activation dumps for the 50 worst queries and share.
Sophia K: if we confirm it's a batching/bucketing bug, it's probably safe to prefer bucket parity as default for int8. downside is potential perf regression — need numbers.
Anita R: initial perf diff is ~3% throughput loss when forcing parity. but cost impact is small compared to user-facing NDCG drop, imo.
Leon T: agree. make the eval gate fail on >2% ndcg regression for non-trivial splits and require a mitigation plan for quantized rollouts.
Anita R: will do. i'll post a short PR with the test and the repro artifacts. thanks all :raised_hands:
Mike L: nice catch. lmk if you want help with activation collection.
Sophia K: ping me when the PR is up, i'll review the eval side.
Anita R: PR link soon.`
